## Whole Orchard Recycling - Space for time 2023

This space for time substitution experiment was conducted in four experimental almond orchards that have whole orchard recycling (WOR) and control treatments. These 4 fields were each sampled in 4 replicate blocks per treatment in Summer 2023 at the University of California Kearney Agricultural Research and Extension Center (UC KARE) located in Fresno County, CA. The soils were first seived to <2 mm and then separated into POM and MAOM fractions. All POM and MAOM samples were air-dried, diluted to 10% (w/w) with pre-ground potassium bromide (KBr), and then analyzed by DRIFTS spectroscopy. Spectral subtractions were performed in OMNIC, to remove the absorbance of inorganic covalent bonds such as Si-O (which compose the mineral contribution of soil).

Space for Time Substitution Design (Fields + Years):
Field K32 (est. 2008) 15 yrs  |   33 tons wood chips/acre   | Blocks 2,3,4,6
Field K74 (est. 2017)  6 yrs  |   85 tons wood chips/acre   | Blocks 11,12,13,14
Field K92 (est. 2019)  4 yrs  |   61 tons wood chips/acre   | Blocks 1,2,3,5
Field K95 (est. 2020)  3 yrs  |   60 tons wood chips/acre   | Blocks 1,2,3,4

POM and MAOM Sample (#) shorthand key:
   [K92]         [K31]        [K74]          [K95]
1. B1 - CN    9.  B2 - CN   17. B11 - CN    25. B1 - CN
2. B2 - CN    10. B3 - CN   18. B12 - CN    26. B2 - CN
3. B3 - CN    11. B4 - CN   19. B13 - CN    27. B3 - CN
4. B5 - CN    12. B6 - CN   20. B14 - CN    28. B4 - CN
5. B1 - WC    13. B2 - WC   21. B11 - WC    29. B1 - WC
6. B2 - WC    14. B3 - WC   22. B12 - WC    30. B2 - WC
7. B3 - WC    15. B4 - WC   23. B13 - WC    31. B3 - WC
8. B5 - WC    16. B6 - WC   24. B14 - WC    32. B4 - WC 
Note: CN = Control, WC = Wood Chip treatments

## Load Libraries and Import the metadata
```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Load Packages
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)   # Provides p-values for lmer models
library(ggplot2)
library(car)
library(DescTools)  
library(rcompanion) # For plotNormalHistogram
library(emmeans)
library(dplyr) # used to filter

# Load the Metadata and Subtraction Index Values
SFT_meta <- readRDS(file = "SFT_2023_Metadata.rds")
SFT_ss_index <- readRDS(file = "Helix_Index123.rds")

# Adjust the class of experimental variables
str(SFT_meta) # Need to convert Treatment, Field, Block, and Year to factors
SFT_meta$Treatment <- as.factor(SFT_meta$Treatment)
SFT_meta$Field <- as.factor(SFT_meta$Field)
SFT_meta$Year_of_WOR <- as.factor(SFT_meta$Year_of_WOR)
SFT_meta$Block_ID <- as.factor(SFT_meta$Block_ID)
```
The SFT_meta dataframe includes is for 32 soil samples (4 fields * 2 treatments * 4 blocks) that were sieved to <2 mm prior to collection of the following data:
- Gravimetric Moisture Content (%)
- Soil pH [20 g of soil + 20 mL of DIW]
- SOM content by LOI (%)
- Water Holding Capacity (%)
- 18O Resipiration Rate (mg CO2 / 24 hrs)
- 16O Respiration Rate (mg Co2 / 24 hrs)
- Dissolved Organic Carbon (mg C / g soil ODW)
- Dissolved Organic Nitrogen (mg N / g soil ODW)
- Microbial Biomass Carbon (mg MBC / g ODW)
- Microbial Biomass Nitrogen (mg MBN / g ODW)
- Total C [of the <2 mm soil] (%)
- Total N [of the <2 mm soil] (%)
- Total C [of the POM fraction] (%)
- Total N [of the POM fraction] (%)
- Total C [of the MAOM fraction] (%)
- Total N [of the MAOM fraction] (%)
- CN_Ratio (TC % / TN %)
- POM_CN_Ratio (POM TC % / POM TN %)
- MAOM_CN_Ratio (MAOM TC % / MAOM TN %)

## Mixed Models - Two-way ANOVAs with lm

# Soil Organic Matter
```{r}
# Fit the model
OM_model <- lm(OM_Content ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta)

# Perform the ANOVA
OM_results <- anova(OM_model)

# Display the ANOVA results
print(OM_results) # Treatment:Field is significant !

# Check residuals of the lm model
plot(OM_model)
qqnorm(residuals(OM_model))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(OM_model))
shapiro.test(residuals(OM_model))  # Shapiro-Wilk test for normality
#W = 0.93441, p-value = 0.05203

# ----------------------------
# TRANSFORMATIONS
# ----------------------------
# Tested Log10, Square-root, Inverse, Cube-root transformations
# Inverse transformation worked best
SFT_meta$inv_SOM <- 1 / SFT_meta$OM_Content
inv_SOM_lm <- lm(inv_SOM ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta)
shapiro.test(residuals(inv_SOM_lm))  # looks best, and highest p-value
# W = 0.98953, p-value = 0.9855
qqnorm(residuals(inv_SOM_lm))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(inv_SOM_lm))

# ------------------------------------
# SOM ANOVA
# ------------------------------------
anova(inv_SOM_lm)
#Response: inv_SOM
#                Df   Sum Sq  Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
#Treatment        1 0.080968 0.080968 41.9446 1.069e-06 ***
#Field            3 0.005625 0.001875  0.9714 0.4224930    
#Treatment:Field  3 0.047486 0.015829  8.1999 0.0006249 ***
#Residuals       24 0.046329 0.001930  

# ----------------------
# POST-HOC PAIRWISE COMPARISONS
# ----------------------
# Compare treatments within each field
SOM_Treatment_PH <- emmeans(inv_SOM_lm, ~ Treatment | Field)
pairwise_contrasts_SOM <- contrast(SOM_Treatment_PH, method = "pairwise")

summary(pairwise_contrasts_SOM)
plot(SOM_Treatment_PH)

#Field = K31:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC   -0.0119 0.0311 24  -0.383  0.7049

#Field = K74:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC    0.1621 0.0311 24   5.217  <.0001 *

#Field = K92:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC    0.1809 0.0311 24   5.823  <.0001 *

#Field = K95:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC    0.0713 0.0311 24   2.296  0.0307 *

SOM_Field_PH <- emmeans(inv_SOM_lm, ~ Field | Treatment)
pairwise_contrasts_SOM <- contrast(SOM_Field_PH, method = "pairwise")
summary(pairwise_contrasts_SOM)
plot(SOM_Field_PH)

#Treatment = CN:
# contrast  estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# K31 - K74  -0.0861 0.0311 24  -2.772  0.0486 *
# K31 - K92  -0.1196 0.0311 24  -3.849  0.0040 *
# K31 - K95  -0.0701 0.0311 24  -2.255  0.1373
# K74 - K92  -0.0335 0.0311 24  -1.078  0.7062
# K74 - K95   0.0161 0.0311 24   0.517  0.9543
# K92 - K95   0.0495 0.0311 24   1.594  0.4006

#Treatment = WC:
# contrast  estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# K31 - K74   0.0879 0.0311 24   2.829  0.0430 *
# K31 - K92   0.0732 0.0311 24   2.357  0.1131
# K31 - K95   0.0132 0.0311 24   0.425  0.9737
# K74 - K92  -0.0146 0.0311 24  -0.472  0.9646
# K74 - K95  -0.0747 0.0311 24  -2.404  0.1033
# K92 - K95  -0.0600 0.0311 24  -1.933  0.2415
```

# Total Carbon
```{r}
# Fit the model
TC_model <- lm(TC ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta)

# Perform the ANOVA
TC_results <- anova(TC_model)

# Display the ANOVA results
print(TC_results) # Year_of_WOR:Treatment is significant !

# Check residuals of the lm model
plot(TC_model)
qqnorm(residuals(TC_model))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(TC_model))
shapiro.test(residuals(TC_model))
# W = 0.94406, p-value = 0.09766

# ----------------------------
# TRANSFORMATIONS
# ----------------------------
# Tested Log10, Square-root, Inverse, Cube-root transformations
# Cube-root transformation worked best
SFT_meta$cbrt_TC <- SFT_meta$TC^(1/3)
cbrt_TC_lm <- lm(cbrt_TC ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta)
shapiro.test(residuals(cbrt_TC_lm)) # looks best, and highest p-value
# W = 0.98767, p-value = 0.9675
qqnorm(residuals(cbrt_TC_lm))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(cbrt_TC_lm))

# ------------------------------------
# TC ANOVA
# ------------------------------------
anova(cbrt_TC_lm)
#Response: cbrt_TC
#                Df   Sum Sq  Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
#Treatment        1 0.146201 0.146201 37.0831 2.735e-06 ***
#Field            3 0.065780 0.021927  5.5616 0.0048241 ** 
#Treatment:Field  3 0.098853 0.032951  8.3579 0.0005585 ***
#Residuals       24 0.094620 0.003943 

# ----------------------
# POST-HOC PAIRWISE COMPARISONS
# ----------------------
# Compare treatments within each field
TC_Treatment_PH <- emmeans(cbrt_TC_lm, ~ Treatment | Field)
pairwise_contrasts_TC <- contrast(TC_Treatment_PH, method = "pairwise")

summary(pairwise_contrasts_TC)
plot(TC_Treatment_PH)

#Field = K31:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC    0.0185 0.0444 24   0.418  0.6800

#Field = K74:

TC_Field_PH <- emmeans(cbrt_TC_lm, ~ Field | Treatment)

summary(pairwise_contrasts_TC)
plot(TC_Field_PH)

#Treatment = CN:
```

# C:N Ratio
```{r}
# Fit the model
CN_model <- lm(CN_Ratio ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta)

# Display the ANOVA results

qqnorm(residuals(CN_model))
```

# POM Total Carbon
```{r}
# Fit the model
POM_TC_model <- lm(POM_TC ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta)

# Perform the ANOVA
POM_TC_results <- anova(POM_TC_model)

# Display the ANOVA results
print(POM_TC_results) # Treatment:Field is significant !

# Check residuals of the lm model
plot(POM_TC_model)
qqnorm(residuals(POM_TC_model))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(POM_TC_model))
shapiro.test(residuals(POM_TC_model))
# W = 0.86485, p-value = 0.0008853

# ----------------------------
# TRANSFORMATIONS
# ----------------------------
# Tested Log10, Square-root, Inverse, Cube-root transformations
# Log10 transformation worked best
SFT_meta$log10_POM_TC <- log10(SFT_meta$POM_TC)
log_POM_TC_lm <- lm(log10_POM_TC ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta)
shapiro.test(residuals(log_POM_TC_lm))  # looks best, and highest p-value
# W = 0.97325, p-value = 0.5935
qqnorm(residuals(log_POM_TC_lm))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(log_POM_TC_lm))

# ------------------------------------
# POM TC ANOVA
# ------------------------------------
anova(log_POM_TC_lm)
#Response: log10_POM_TC
#                Df  Sum Sq Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
#Treatment        1 0.55599 0.55599 39.0464 1.854e-06 ***
#Field            3 0.59978 0.19993 14.0406 1.718e-05 ***
#Treatment:Field  3 0.40102 0.13367  9.3877 0.0002749 ***
#Residuals       24 0.34174 0.01424 

# ----------------------
# POST-HOC PAIRWISE COMPARISONS
# ----------------------
# Compare treatments within each field
POM_TC_Treatment_PH <- emmeans(log_POM_TC_lm, ~ Treatment | Field)
pairwise_contrasts_POM_TC <- contrast(POM_TC_Treatment_PH, method = "pairwise")

summary(pairwise_contrasts_POM_TC)
plot(POM_TC_Treatment_PH)
```

## Helix 2026 Indices, Revised for Wood (aromatic hydrocarbon) Amendment
# Spectral Index Values Decomposition (1) and Recalcitrance (2) Index Values

# Index 1 (Aliphatic : Aromatic) and 2 (Aromatic : Carboxylic),
In accordance with the wavenumber corresponding to the 13 organic bands described in Margenot et al 2015: https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.2136/sssaj2015.02.0070

Index 1 = (2931 + 2871) / (1660 + 1600 + 1540 + 1510)
# ( Aliphatic : Aromatic )

Index 2 = (1660 + 1600 + 1540 + 1510) / (1724 + 1320 + 1275)
# ( Aromatic : Carboxylic )

# Note:
Sample POM 4 (K92_B5_CN) needs to be removed before the following model fitting can be performed. Essentially, the spectral subtraction for this sample yielded negative peaks, and the resulting Index values are sometimes "Inf", NA, or 0.000. This samples is clearly an outlier, and is impeding ANOVA due to the following error:

anova_model_main <- lm(POM_Decomposition_Index ~ Field + Treatment, data = SFT_meta)
Error in lm.fit(x, y, offset = offset, singular.ok = singular.ok, ...) : 
  NA/NaN/Inf in 'y'

Due to the structure of the data table (Sample ID as rows, with POM and MAOM values as columns), the simplest solution is to create a copy of the metadata, with the problematic POM sample removed:
```{r}
# Create a filtered dataset only for POM analysis
SFT_meta_POM <- SFT_meta %>%
  filter(Sample != "K92_B5_CN")  # exclude bad sample
```

# POM Index 1 (Decomposition) Helix (outliers filtered)
# (Aliphatic : Aromatic) Index
```{r}
# POM Decomposition
# ------------------------------------
# Outlier removal (IQR) for POM Decomposition Index
# ------------------------------------
remove_outliers <- function(x) {
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  IQR <- Q3 - Q1
  x[x < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | x > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)] <- NA
  return(x)
}
SFT_meta_POM$POM_Decomposition_Index_filtered <- remove_outliers(SFT_meta_POM$POM_Decomposition_Index)

# Fit the model
POM_1_model <- lm(POM_Decomposition_Index_filtered ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta_POM)
POM_1_results <- anova(POM_1_model)
print(POM_1_results) # Year_of_WOR:Treatment is significant!

# Residual diagnostics
plot(POM_1_model)
qqnorm(residuals(POM_1_model))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(POM_1_model))
shapiro.test(residuals(POM_1_model))
# W = 0.95636, p-value = 0.2666

# ----------------------------
# TRANSFORMATIONS
# ----------------------------
# Tested Log10, Square-root, Inverse, Cube-root transformations
# Cube-root transformation worked best
SFT_meta_POM$cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index <- SFT_meta_POM$POM_Decomposition_Index_filtered^(1/3)
cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index_lm <- lm(cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta_POM)
shapiro.test(residuals(cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index_lm))
# W = 0.98392, p-value = 0.9246
qqnorm(residuals(cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index_lm))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index_lm))

# ------------------------------------
# POM index 1 ANOVA (Aliphatic : Aromatic)
# ------------------------------------
anova(cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index_lm)
#Response: cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index
#                Df  Sum Sq  Mean Sq F value    Pr(>F)    
#Treatment        1 0.01886 0.018864  1.0552 0.3160013    
#Field            3 0.60464 0.201548 11.2741 0.0001285 ***
#Treatment:Field  3 0.18632 0.062107  3.4741 0.0342667 *  
#Residuals       21 0.37542 0.017877                      

POM_Decomposition_Index_Treatment_PH <- emmeans(cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index_lm, ~ Treatment | Field)
pairwise_contrasts_POM_Decomposition_Index <- contrast(POM_Decomposition_Index_Treatment_PH, method = "pairwise")
summary(pairwise_contrasts_POM_Decomposition_Index)
plot(POM_Decomposition_Index_Treatment_PH)

#Field = K31:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC  -0.02968 0.0945 21  -0.314  0.7567

#Field = K74:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC   0.19905 0.1020 21   1.949  0.0648

#Field = K92:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC  -0.29868 0.1160 21  -2.579  0.0175 *

#Field = K95:
# contrast estimate     SE df t.ratio p.value
# CN - WC  -0.00678 0.0945 21  -0.072  0.9435

# Extract significant post-hoc contrasts – Treatment within Field
pom_decomp_treatment_sig <- as.data.frame(summary(pairwise_contrasts_POM_Decomposition_Index)) %>%
  filter(p.value < 0.05) %>%
  mutate(Parameter = "POM_Decomposition_Index")

POM_Decomposition_Index_Field_PH <- emmeans(cbrt_POM_Decomposition_Index_lm, ~ Field | Treatment)
pairwise_contrasts_POM_Decomposition_Index <- contrast(POM_Decomposition_Index_Field_PH, method = "pairwise")
summary(pairwise_contrasts_POM_Decomposition_Index)
plot(POM_Decomposition_Index_Field_PH)
```

```{r}
MAOM_Decomposition_Index_Field_PH <- emmeans(MAOM_1_model, ~ Field | Treatment)

plot(MAOM_Decomposition_Index_Field_PH)
```

# MAOM Index 2 (Recalcitrance) Helix (outliers filtered)
# ( Aromatic : Carboxylic ) Index
```{r}
# MAOM Recalcitrance
# ------------------------------------
# Outlier removal (IQR) for MAOM Recalcitrance Index
# ------------------------------------
remove_outliers <- function(x) {
  Q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  Q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  IQR <- Q3 - Q1
  x[x < (Q1 - 1.5 * IQR) | x > (Q3 + 1.5 * IQR)] <- NA
  return(x)
}
SFT_meta$MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_filtered <- remove_outliers(SFT_meta$MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index)

# Fit the model
MAOM_2_model <- lm(MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_filtered ~ Field * Treatment, data = SFT_meta)
MAOM_2_results <- anova(MAOM_2_model)
print(MAOM_2_results)

# Check residuals of the lm model
plot(MAOM_2_model)
qqnorm(residuals(MAOM_2_model))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(MAOM_2_model))
shapiro.test(residuals(MAOM_2_model))
# W = 0.98297, p-value = 0.8889

# ----------------------------
# TRANSFORMATIONS
# ----------------------------
# Tested Log10, Square-root, Inverse, Cube-root transformations
# Square-root transformation worked best
SFT_meta$sqrt_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index <- sqrt(SFT_meta$MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_filtered)
sqrt_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_lm <- lm(sqrt_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index ~ Treatment * Field, data = SFT_meta)
shapiro.test(residuals(sqrt_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_lm))
# W = 0.98405, p-value = 0.9127
qqnorm(residuals(sqrt_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_lm))
plotNormalHistogram(residuals(sqrt_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_lm))

# ------------------------------------
# MAOM index 2 ANOVA ( Aromatic : Carboxylic )
# ------------------------------------
anova(sqrt_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_lm)

MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_Treatment_PH <- emmeans(sqrt_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_lm, ~ Treatment | Field)
pairwise_contrasts_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index <- contrast(MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index_Treatment_PH, method = "pairwise")
summary(pairwise_contrasts_MAOM_Recalcitrance_Index)
```
